questions.title: Which club will Ferran Torres join from Barcelona during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Ferran Torres is a Barcelona forward and Spain international.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official club announcements or confirmed reporting from reputable sports news outlets. Resolution : Resolve to the first club Ferran Torres joins directly from Barcelona during the 2026 summer transfer window. The move must be confirmed as completed; transfer rumors, negotiations, and expressions of interest do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The destination club's name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-08 update (ESPN Aug 8, Le Parisien/L'Equipe/MARCA Aug 8, FootballTransfers/Ben Jacobs Aug 8, GiveMeSport/CaughtOffside Aug 7, local Al Jazeera & Straits Times Aug 8): Major convergence of Tier-1 reporting confirms Ferran Torres has agreed personal terms on a 5-year contract with Paris Saint-Germain and formally informed Barcelona he wants to join PSG to reunite with Luis Enrique; Barcelona will not stand in his way (avoiding an EUR 8m Man City renewal bonus clause with 1 year left on his deal) and PSG are prepared to pay ~EUR 50m, with all parties aiming to close a deal before Torres's Wednesday Aug 12 training return. Because ESPN and Le Parisien note formal club-to-club fee agreement is not yet completed (Barca awaiting PSG's first formal offer / opening talks), lifting PSG from 0.62 -> 0.65 while strictly observing our 0.65 unconfirmed-transfer ceiling. Behind PSG, Atletico Madrid drop sharply (0.12 -> 0.07) after coach Diego Simeone and CEO Miguel Angel Gil Marin publicly declared on Aug 8 that Julian Alvarez is not for sale at any price (undercutting swap speculation), while Arsenal rise to #2 (0.06 -> 0.10) after Aug 7 reporting that Arsenal held talks with Torres's representatives as a Vinicius Jr alternative; trimming quiet Tottenham Hotspur (0.09 -> 0.07) and holding Aston Villa (0.04). Sum 0.93 leaves 7% residual.

local_articles.title: PSG sign France defender Lucal Digne from Aston Villa on three-year contract
local_articles.snippet: Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne has joined Paris Saint-Germain on a three-year deal, the European champions announced on Aug 9. The 33-year-old French international, who grew up in the Paris region, returns to PSG, where he played for two seasons between 2013 and 2015. “I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain,” Digne said in a statement on the Ligue 1 champions’ website. “I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years. “I can’t wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team.” After PSG, Digne spent time on loan in Serie A with Roma before signing for Spanish giants Barcelona, who were then coached by current PSG boss Luis Enrique. questions.title: Which stadium will Shakhtar Donetsk announce an agreement to use for its home matches in the main phase of the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League?
questions.background: War has prevented Shakhtar Donetsk from hosting European matches in Ukraine, forcing the club to arrange alternative venues abroad.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official Shakhtar Donetsk announcement, or reliable reporting quoting the club, identifying its agreed home venue for the 2026–27 Champions League main phase. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the stadium named in the first such agreement announced by August 31, 2026. The announcement determines the answer; subsequent regulatory approval or the actual staging of matches is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The stadium’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Complete venue overhaul driven by June 24 - July 26 reporting (BBC Sport, City AM, The Athletic via talkSPORT, Evening Standard, and UNN/Suspilne Sport): Shakhtar officially stated they are negotiating with venues in the UK and Germany (dropping Poland after Wisla Krakow's refusal), and on July 26 Shakhtar head coach Arda Turan explicitly announced 'It looks like we will play our European Cup matches in London... We are also waiting for everyone in London.' Three West London Premier League clubs with no 2026-27 European football have held talks: Brentford's Gtech Community Stadium (0.28 — earliest/longest-documented talks since June 24, established third-party rental model, UEFA compliant), Chelsea's Stamford Bridge (0.26 — 40k turnkey UCL venue, Chelsea seeking non-European revenue after finishing 10th), and Fulham's Craven Cottage (0.23 — renovated Riverside Stand and strong Shakhtar-Fulham relationship from the Kevin transfer). Keeping Veltins-Arena (0.06) as the top German fallback if London policing/council permits stall, and London Stadium (0.04) as an unconfirmed London UEFA Cat 4 fallback with West Ham in the Championship (sum 0.87, leaving 13% for other German/London venues).

questions.title: Which European country will announce a complete drought-related shutdown of its nuclear power generation between August 1 and August 13, 2026?
questions.background: Nuclear reactors require reliable cooling-water supplies. Low river levels can force reactors to shut down, potentially disrupting national electricity supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements by national nuclear operators or governments, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Identify the European country that announces, between August 1 and August 13, 2026, a shutdown covering its entire operating nuclear fleet because drought has left insufficient river water for cooling. An announcement initiating the shutdown of the last operating reactor qualifies; a partial shutdown alone does not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-09 update (Exa searches Aug 6-9: AP News Aug 6, L'Express Aug 6, New Scientist Aug 7; local Arab News/Reuters Aug 6, Khaleej Times Aug 8, CBS News Aug 8, Al Jazeera Aug 9): Neither Romania nor Hungary has announced a complete fleet shutdown through Sunday Aug 9 (note: an NDTV/AFP wire crawled Aug 5 with an Aug 9 publish tag erroneously conflated earlier warnings as completed shutdowns, contradicted by Aug 6-8 Reuters, AP, and Khaleej Times reporting). Nudging Romania up 0.58 -> 0.62 and trimming Hungary 0.35 -> 0.31 with only four days left in the Aug 1-13 window: (1) Romania delayed sinking its four rock-filled Danube barges until Friday Aug 7 citing unsafe conditions as lower-Danube flow hit an all-time low of 1,400 m3/s, with Cernavoda director Romeo Urjan warning Unit 2 faces shutdown in 5-6 days (Aug 11-12, squarely inside the window) unless the submerged barrier yields surplus water and upstream Serbian meteorologists (Khaleej Times Aug 8) reporting no meaningful rainfall recovery in sight; (2) Hungary's Paks has now survived five consecutive days since Tuesday's 1 mm near-miss, clearing the Friday Aug 7 cold front and Aug 8-9 weekend without a shutdown announcement (with PM Peter Magyar describing Paks as 'nearly forced' offline on Thursday and pivoting Saturday to nominating Andras Baka for Hungary's presidency, Al Jazeera Aug 9). Retaining substantial 0.31 weight on Hungary because Paks remains on a single reduced-output turbine (~10% capacity) into a dry stretch plus residual interpretation risk from Magyar's Aug 1-2 warnings, while holding Bulgaria 0.035, Slovenia 0.02, and Switzerland 0.005 (sum 0.99, keeping Romania below the 0.65 unconfirmed-event cap).

Resolution : Resolve when AP identifies the candidate who has secured the nomination. A preliminary lead or advancement to a runoff does not count as winning the nomination.
